title: Search measure
statement: For a natural number $n$ and a Boolean list $S$, let $a$ be the first component of the default pair decomposition of $S$, let $b$ be the first component of the default pair decomposition of the second component of $S$, and let $	au$ be the first entry of the second component of that second component, taking $	au$ to be false if the component is empty. Define the search measure to be $0$ when $	au$ is true; otherwise define it as $(P(n)-v(a))(P(n)+1)+(v(a)-v(b))+1$, where $P(n)$ is the prime-valued function used in the definition and $v$ is the binary value of a Boolean list.
caveat: The supplied material does not define the default pair decomposition, the binary-value convention, or the prime-valued function, so their meanings cannot be made fully self-contained from the given definitions.
